candidate_sentences.text: Nordecon AS reported a consolidated revenue of 208.3 million euros for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, representing a seven percent decrease from the 223.9 million euros recorded in 2024.
The group’s gross margin contracted by one percentage point to 6.5 percent, down from 7.5 percent in the prior year, with the Buildings segment margin falling from 8.9 percent to 7.7 percent.
Consequently, operating profit declined to 5.7 million euros from 8.1 million euros in 2024, leading to an operating margin of 2.7 percent compared to 3.6 percent previously.

Net profit for the period was 2.5 million euros, a significant reduction from 5.2 million euros in 2024, largely impacted by a 750 thousand euro foreign exchange loss caused by the weakening of the Ukrainian hryvnia against the euro.
The exchange rate of the hryvnia weakened by approximately 12 percent during the year, contributing to higher finance costs that totaled 3.5 million euros.

verified_key_information_units.information: Year-on-year segment revenue changes showed the Buildings segment decreasing approximately 10% while the Infrastructure segment increased approximately 10%, resulting in Buildings contributing 81% of total revenue (down from 84%) and Infrastructure 19% (up from 16%).

candidate_sentences.text: This decline was primarily driven by a ten percent drop in the Buildings segment, which accounted for 81 percent of total revenue, while the Infrastructure segment saw a ten percent growth.

verified_key_information_units.information: The order book grew by 30% to €273.1m at year-end, driven by a nearly threefold increase in the Infrastructure segment order book; approximately 69% of the backlog relates to work scheduled for 2026, with the remainder spread across 2027-2028.

candidate_sentences.text: Despite the lower profitability, the group’s order book grew substantially by 30 percent to 273.1 million euros at year-end, up from 209.5 million euros in 2024.
This growth was driven by a nearly threefold increase in the Infrastructure segment’s order book, which now comprises 42 percent of the total backlog, compared to 18 percent in the previous year.
Approximately 69 percent of the current order book is scheduled for execution in 2026, providing visibility for future revenue.

verified_key_information_units.information: Cash flows for 2025 included €1.2m net cash from operating activities, €2.8m net cash used in investing activities (including €2.9m placed in long-term deposits), and €1.2m net cash used in financing activities, resulting in a net cash outflow of €2.8m for the year.

details.completeness_justification: All six key information units are adequately represented in the candidate summary. K1 is covered through S1 (revenue decline), S3 (gross margin), S5 (operating margin), S6 (net profit), and S7 (foreign exchange loss). K2 is fully covered by S2 (segment revenue changes and contributions). K3 is covered by S8 (order book growth), S9 (Infrastructure segment increase), and S12 (2026 schedule). K4 is covered by S13 (operating cash inflow), S14 (investing/financing outflows). K5 is covered by S15 (cash equivalents) and S16 (current ratio). K6 is covered by S18 (stable employee count and staff cost reduction). No material omissions affect the overall understanding.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected, with no self-contradictions. The summary follows a clear structure: revenue performance, margin analysis, expense management, profitability, order book growth, cash flow, liquidity, and workforce efficiency. Explanations for changes (e.g., foreign exchange loss, staff cost reductions) are consistent with the reported outcomes. There is no unnecessary repetition, and all relationships between segments, margins, and profits are logically presented without internal inconsistency. The arithmetic differences between segment and consolidated figures are not claimed to be directly additive, so they do not constitute contradictions under the evaluation constraints.
